Marta (support): FYI customer on Dedicated is seeing flaky SSE streams after a token refresh. They get empty/"" chunks from the Python iterator, then a 502 on reconnect. Reports started after they upgraded to our Python SDK 0.8.0.

Marta (support): Example from customer logs (copied):
```
client: py-sdk==0.8.0
loop: async iterator over StreamingClient.stream_generate
observed chunks: '\n', '', 'here-is-token', '', ''
error on reconnect: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway
```

Marta (support): Their minimal repro (pseudo):
```python
from redwood import StreamingClient
client = StreamingClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
for chunk in client.stream_generate(model='rwd-1', prompt='hello'):
    print(repr(chunk))
# sometimes prints '' or '\n' and then raises on reconnect
```

Ethan (py-sdk): thanks — can you get me the exact chunk prints and the client-side exception stack? Also want the server SSE trace (headers + raw event lines) if possible.

Marta (support): pasted raw SSE from customer (sanitized):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

data: {"id":"tok-1","delta":"Hel"}

data: 

data: {"delta":"lo"}

data: 

data: {"delta":"\""}


# then connection reset and 502 on reconnect
```

Lina (ingest): that pattern looks like repeated empty data events interspersed — we've seen this when the SSE read loop yields an empty chunk on partial flush + client-side buffer not reset. Could be the iterator's internal buffer retaining state across reconnects.

Ravi (sre): customer provided curl reproduction too: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=rwd-1` — they saw intermittent `HTTP/1.1 502` after ~15s. Network trace shows `ConnectionResetError` from upstream.

Ethan (py-sdk): I have a hypothesis: we added async buffering for performance in 0.8.0 and changed the reconnect path to reuse the same iterator object. If a reconnect happens while buffer contains a newline-only chunk, the iterator yields an empty string then later yields the remainder — results in duplicates/empty chunks and sometimes an exception when the reconnect handling tries to parse an already-closed stream.

Ethan (py-sdk): Quick repro I ran locally (same pattern) — failing with the iterator returning `''` entries. Patch idea: on any ConnectionResetError in the SSE read loop, clear the internal chunk buffer and emit a synthetic keepalive only if non-empty, then reopen the connection.

Marta (support): customer asked for workaround until patch is released.

Lina (ingest): temporary workaround: have them pin `py-sdk==0.7.3` (last known good) OR set env `RW_SDK_STREAM_FLUSH=1` which will force the SDK to drop empty chunks on reconnect. Not ideal but quick.

Ethan (py-sdk): I pushed a targeted fix to reset iterator buffer on reconnect (PR #433). Test wheel available: `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk@8f3c9ad#egg=redwood-sdk` — commit 8f3c9ad. It explicitly clears `_pending_chunk` on ConnectionResetError and avoids yielding empty strings.

Marta (support): pushed the test wheel to the customer; they report it reduced empty chunks and reconnects. They still saw one 502 but stream resumed when retry policy kicked in.

Ravi (sre): server traces show one upstream reset coincident with their token rotation window. We'll add extra logging around connection termination cause.

Ethan (py-sdk): Follow-up items:
- roll fix into 0.8.1 release (include changelog entry about buffer reset on reconnect)
- add unit tests for empty-chunk sequences + reconnect handling in async iterator
- add telemetry to mark how often we see empty chunks pre/post-release

Marta (support): Customer accepted workaround and will upgrade when we release 0.8.1. They requested ETA — please aim for tomorrow's patch release.

Ethan (py-sdk): ACK — will cut 0.8.1 after CI. I will post the release notes here.
